1. What the Site is

The Site tells you about Pawstcard, a report-card tool for pet sitters, publishes a Journal of articles for independent pet sitters and dog walkers, and lets you join an early-access waitlist.

2. The early-access waitlist

Joining the waitlist means you would like to be invited to the beta. It is not an account, a purchase, or a contract for the app. We may change, delay or cancel the beta or the launch, and we do not promise an invitation or a date.

Prices and "founding" rates shown on the Site (for example "$12/month, locked in for life for early-access members" and "free during beta") describe our current plans. They are not a binding offer until you accept the app's own terms.

How we handle your email address is described in our Privacy Policy.

3. The Pawstcard app (not yet released)

So that nobody is surprised later, this is what we say today about the app. The full terms will come with the app.

  • Pawstcard drafts a visit note from your photos and taps. You can edit every word, and nothing is sent until you approve it.
  • Medication entries use fixed wording instead of AI.

4. Journal content: general guidance only

Journal articles are general guidance for independent pet sitters and dog walkers. They are not legal, veterinary, tax, financial or other professional advice. Rules about contracts, fees, insurance, medication, authorizing veterinary care and similar topics vary by place and situation. Check what applies to you, follow your clients' and vets' instructions, and talk to a qualified professional where needed.
